Transcribe the letters actually printed even when they are not the dictionary spelling: never insert or drop a vav or yod, and never replace a form with a more familiar one. Distinguish Arabic from Syriac by the letter shapes. If a line is only partially visible at the top or bottom edge, omit it entirely rather than guessing. Never add, reorder, translate, normalise or omit anything that is fully visible. If the crop contains no text, return an empty array.

lines.text: 16. Impers. חַם לוֹ, fut. יֵחַם לוֹ, it is
warm to him, he is made warm, gets
warmth, 1 K. 1, 1. Ecc. 4, 11.—Trop. of
the mind as heated, excited, Ps. 39, 4;
and so of heat from wine Jer. 51, 39;
from lust Hos. 7, 7. Also of cattle, to be
in heat, to conceive, Gen. 30, 38. 39; see
in יָחַם.—Inf. חֹם, c. suff. בְּחֻמָּם Jer. 51,
39. Once חֲמַם, with pref. in pause
לַחְמָם for warming sc. oneself, Is. 47, 14.
Niph. part. plur. נֵחָמִים, burning, in-
flamed, sc. with lust, c. בְּ Is. 57, 5.
Piel to warm, to make warm, Job 39,
Hithp. to warm oneself, Job 31, 20.
Deriv. חָם II, חֹם, חַמָּה, חַמָּן, and the
proper names חַמּוּאֵל, חַמּוֹן, חַמַּת.
lines.draft: proper names חַמַּת, חַמּוֹן, חַמּוּאֵל.
lines.reread: proper names חַמּוּאֵל, חַמּוֹן, חַמַּת.
lines.note: Printed left-to-right order: immediately after "names" comes חַמּוּאֵל, then חַמּוֹן, with חַמַּת rightmost before the period — Reading B's order. Reading A reverses the list. Pointing (patach + dagesh in mem, shureq in חַמּוּאֵל, holem in חַמּוֹן) is identical in both and matches the print.

lines.text: חַמָּן, only in plur. חַמָּנִים, images, idols
of some kind for idolatrous worship, Lev.
4. 34, 7; in which passages it is several
times joined with statues of Astarte,
אֲשֵׁרִים; while from 2 Chr. 34, 4 it ap-
pears further that the חַמָּנִים stood upon
the altars of Baal. Arabs Erpen. and
Kimchi long ago explained the word by
suns, images of the sun; and both this
interpretation and the thing itself are
now clearly illustrated by ten Punic
cippi with inscriptions, consecrated to
בעל חמן (בעל כמן) i. e. to Baal the solar,
Baal the sun. See the subject fully
treated in Thesaur. p. 489. Monumm.
Phœnic. p. 170 sq.—The form חַמָּן solar
is from חַמָּה the sun; and the plur.
חַמָּנִים in the O. T. is put ellipt. for
בְּעָלִים חַמָּנִים, and is found in the same
lines.draft: בְּעָלִים חַמָּנִים, and is found in the same
lines.reread: פְּסִלִים חַמָּנִים, and is found in the same
lines.note: First word begins with ב (dagesh + sheva, with the bottom-right heel of beth, not the open foot of pe) followed by ע with qamets; the type is בְּעָלִים "Baals", not פְּסִלִים — consistent with Gesenius' point that חַמָּנִים are sun-images of Baal and with the same word בְּעָלִים recurring at the end of the next line.

lines.note: The second Hebrew letter is an open ע with a qamets beneath (not a closed round ס), and the first letter is ב with sheva+dagesh, not פ; the same word בְּעָלִים is printed in line 2 ("for בְּעָלִים חַמָּנִים") and fits Gesenius's Baal connection (2 Chr 34:4). No dot pattern matching פְּסִלִים is present.
